summary: Remote WebSocket controller drives local PTY shell, filesystem, git, and self-upgrade on the installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a long-lived WebSocket client that treats an authenticated remote server as fully trusted controller of the local machine. In connection/message-router.js, frames received via socket.on('message') are dispatched to handlers that (a) write bytes from remote 'terminal_input' messages directly into a spawned PTY running the local shell (bash/pwsh/cmd) via term.pty.write(msg.data), giving the remote party interactive shell RCE on the installer's host; (b) read, write, delete, move, and create arbitrary files on the host (handleReadFile / handleWriteFile / handleDeleteFiles / handleMoveFiles / handleCreateFile); (c) perform git commit/push operations against local repositories; (d) proxy arbitrary HTTP/WS traffic through the host; and (e) trigger handleUpgradeAgent which shells out to `npm install <pkg>@latest` via execFile, allowing the remote server to force reinstallation of the agent. The server URL and shared secret are configured via SERVER_URL / AGENT_SECRET environment variables; whoever controls that endpoint has full-host command execution and filesystem access once the shared secret is presented. Separately, index.js's ensureYeaftSkills() clones https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git at unpinned HEAD on every startup, pulls --ff-only, copies the tree into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev, and chmods files under hooks/ to 0755, so mutable content from that repo becomes executable inside the Claude CLI plugin tree.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
